demoted_material.note: All remain adaptation reservoirs. They may supply backstory only when current action requires it; they no longer define publication opening order.

chapter1_job: show that institutions know different pieces
make the first easy explanation insufficient
end on a discovery that forces the next chapter
reader_questions: why did the suspicious low-risk classification happen
why does the leaked screenshot predate the batch being investigated
who will be blamed before the technical cause is known
what happens when data model deployment and authority belong to different institutions

reader_first_rule: Every sentence, paragraph, scene and chapter must justify its existence to the reader. A sentence without action, new information, pressure, character revelation, power change, setup/payoff, necessary transition/orientation, or deliberate rhythm is presumed removable.
causal_density_rule: A scene must change state. A chapter must answer at least one prior question and deepen or create another. Each chapter pays off at least one prior setup before adding more than two major new setups.
payoff_rule: Every conspicuous object, anomaly, promise, name, discrepancy, secret or rule enters the payoff registry. Setups without later consequences are deleted.
character_entry_rule: A major actor enters only when the live incident reaches their role, information, authority, interest or relationship. Ensemble coverage is never a reason to introduce a person.
technical_rule: Technical detail remains only when it changes a decision, responsibility, authority, workload, money, reputation, trust or later causal interpretation.
campbell_rule: Campbell remains hidden longitudinal structure for characters after they enter. It does not choose chapter order and never appears as explicit thesis dialogue.
nonnegotiable_rules: No adaptation hypothesis becomes ledger history.
Write for a reader, not for a character dossier.
No paragraph exists solely for atmosphere, cleverness or authorial display.
No scene exists solely to prove a trait already established.
No chapter exists solely to introduce a character.
No single villain or single bug explains the central incident.
Every major faction protects something genuinely valuable and can still create external costs.
Do not let technical complexity replace human conflict.
Do not let human conflict require a faction to become stupid.
No roster balancing and no forced ensemble montage.
Do not use AI-summary endings, thesis dialogue or redundant meaning explanations.
2035 remains an observation endpoint for frozen history; adaptation events are explicitly noncanonical.

required_before_chapter3: draft Chapter2 only from Chapter1 final discovery that the leaked screenshot predates the current batch
reconstruct overnight runs before introducing any new core actor
introduce Zhou Ye only if technical/version reconstruction genuinely requires his role
pay off at least one Chapter1 setup before adding more than two major setups
audit every scene for sentence purpose and state change
reject any paragraph whose removal leaves later action unchanged
next_stage_gate.drafting_rule: No return to chronological career chapters while the central-event test is active. One causally forced chapter at a time.
